title: SIU probes death of man sought in stabbing
article: Ontario's Special Investigations Unit has been called in to probe the fatal police shooting of a man suspected in a multiple stabbing that killed a nine-year-old boy and injured two others.

Andrew Osidacz, 41, was shot Saturday evening after a confrontation with two Brantford, Ont., police officers at an area home, the SIU said in a statement yesterday. He was later pronounced dead in hospital.
Officers had responded to a domestic dispute call, where they discovered a woman and two children had been stabbed, police said.
"The eight-year-old girl has been hospitalized with non-life-threatening injuries, and the nine-year-old boy is deceased," Brantford police Sergeant Rob Dinner said yesterday.
The woman, whose age is not known, was also taken to hospital with non-life-threatening injuries, Sgt. Dinner said.

Mr. Osidacz had fled the scene before police arrived, but officers found him at a second residence about two kilometres away. He was shot during a confrontation with police and later died in hospital. There were few details available yesterday about what led investigators to the second home or the circumstances of the shooting.

Police did not release the names of the victims, and investigators would not confirm their relationship to Mr. Osidacz, but Global News reported yesterday he was the children's father and the woman's boyfriend.

"This is an incident of domestic violence, so there is a relationship -- either a familial relationship or a romantic nature," Brantford police Inspector Scott Easto told the Toronto news station CP24.
The case has left police and the entire community stunned, but the officers involved in the shooting are coping, Sgt. Dinner said.
"I think everybody's doing the best they can, under the circumstances," he said.
A post-mortem on Mr. Osidacz's body was scheduled for yesterday, the SIU said in a news release.
The SIU is a civilian agency that investigates circumstances involving police and civilians that have resulted in serious injury, sexual assault or death.
